input:
∫ dx/(sin x + cos x) =

Options:
A. √2 log(x + π/4) + c, where c is a constant of integration.
B. (1/√2) log(tan(x/2 + π/8)) + c, where c is a constant of integration.
C. (1/√2) log((tan(x/2) - √2+1)/(tan(x/2) + √2+1)) + c, where c is a constant of integration.
D. -(1/√2) log((tan(x/2) - (√2+1))/(tan(x/2) + √2-1)) + c, where c is a constant of integration.

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate ∫ dx/(sin x + cos x) using the Weierstrass half-angle substitution t = tan(x/2).
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Use the universal substitution t = tan(x/2): sin x = 2t/(1+t²), cos x = (1-t²)/(1+t²), dx = 2dt/(1+t²). This converts the integral to a rational function of t, which can be handled as a difference of squares.

key_concepts: Rational integration of 1/(a² - u²) using partial fractions

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute t = tan(x/2), simplify sin x + cos x in terms of t, reduce to ∫ 2/(2t+1-t²) dt, rewrite as ∫ -2/(t²-2t-1) dt, complete the square in the denominator, and apply the standard formula.
logical_steps: Step 1: Substitute t = tan(x/2), express sin x, cos x, dx
Step 2: Write sin x + cos x in terms of t
Step 3: Simplify the integral to ∫ 2/(2t+1-t²) dt
Step 6: Apply the log formula and substitute back t = tan(x/2)
